sources.entry: markitdown - Python tool for converting files and office documents to Markdown.

summary.one_liner: MarkItDown is a Python library and command-line tool from Microsoft that converts files such as PDF, Office documents, images, audio, HTML, and YouTube URLs into Markdown for LLM and text-analysis pipelines.
summary.what_it_does: The tool converts many input types to Markdown while trying to preserve structure such as headings, lists, tables, and links. Supported inputs named in the README include PDF, PowerPoint, Word, Excel, images (EXIF metadata and OCR), audio (EXIF metadata and speech transcription), HTML, CSV, JSON, XML, ZIP archives (iterating over contents), YouTube URLs, and EPub. It can be used from Python via a MarkItDown class with convert methods (convert_local, convert_stream, convert_response) or from the markitdown CLI, including piping content in. Optional dependency groups (for example [pdf], [docx], [pptx]) keep installs lean. It also supports third-party plugins, which are disabled by default, and optional Azure Document Intelligence and Azure Content Understanding backends, plus LLM-generated image descriptions when an OpenAI-compatible client is provided.
use_cases: Convert PDFs and Word documents to Markdown for LLM input
Extract text and tables from Excel or PowerPoint files
Turn HTML pages or YouTube videos into text for analysis
Batch-convert a folder of mixed office files for a RAG pipeline
Generate image descriptions with a vision-capable LLM
notable: Output is Markdown designed for LLM consumption, not high-fidelity human-facing conversion
Modular optional extras so only needed format dependencies are installed
Third-party plugin system with a markitdown-ocr plugin for LLM-vision OCR of embedded images
Azure Document Intelligence and Content Understanding backends add structured fields as YAML front matter
Security guidance on narrowest convert_* method for untrusted input
caveats: Performs I/O with the privileges of the running process; untrusted inputs must be sanitized
Azure backends are billable cloud API calls; Content Understanding is the only video option
Built-in converters offer only basic audio transcription and no video support
Not intended as a high-fidelity converter for human reading
